title: 08. Files & Errors: 05 — Exception Handling (Deep Dive)
summary: Never except: or except BaseException: — you'd swallow Ctrl+C and SystemExit.

sections.title: 1. Hierarchy
sections.body:
```
BaseException
 ├── SystemExit
 ├── KeyboardInterrupt
 ├── GeneratorExit
 └── Exception                           ← catch this, never BaseException
      ├── ArithmeticError
      │   ├── ZeroDivisionError
      │   ├── OverflowError
      │   └── FloatingPointError
      ├── AssertionError
      ├── AttributeError
      ├── BufferError
      ├── EOFError
      ├── ImportError / ModuleNotFoundError
      ├── LookupError
      │   ├── IndexError
      │   └── KeyError
      ├── MemoryError
      ├── NameError / UnboundLocalError
      ├── OSError
      │   ├── FileNotFoundError
      │   ├── FileExistsError
      │   ├── PermissionError
      │   ├── IsADirectoryError
      │   ├── NotADirectoryError
      │   ├── ConnectionError
      │   │   ├── ConnectionAbortedError
      │   │   ├── ConnectionRefusedError
      │   │   ├── ConnectionResetError
      │   │   └── BrokenPipeError
      │   └── TimeoutError
      ├── RecursionError
      ├── ReferenceError
      ├── RuntimeError
      ├── StopIteration / StopAsyncIteration
      ├── SyntaxError / IndentationError / TabError
      ├── SystemError
      ├── TypeError
      ├── ValueError / UnicodeError / UnicodeDecodeError / UnicodeEncodeError
      └── Warning (DeprecationWarning, ResourceWarning, ...)
```

**Never** `except:` or `except BaseException:` — you'd swallow Ctrl+C and `SystemExit`.

sections.title: 2. try / except / else / finally
sections.body:
```python
try:
    risky()
except (KeyError, ValueError) as e:
    log(e)                                 # multiple types
except Exception as e:
    log("unexpected", e)
    raise                                  # re-raise to not hide bugs
else:
    commit()                               # runs only if no exception
finally:
    cleanup()                              # always runs
```

- **`else`** — body runs only if `try` completed without raising. Keeps `try` block small (only the line that may raise).
- **`finally`** — cleanup; runs even if `try` had `return`, `break`, `continue`, or raised.

### Order of catch blocks

Subclasses first, parents last. `except OSError` before `except FileNotFoundError` would shadow the latter.

sections.title: 3. Raising
sections.body:
```python
raise ValueError("bad input")
raise ValueError("bad input") from e       # chain (sets __cause__)
raise ValueError("bad input") from None    # suppress chaining
raise                                       # re-raise current
```

- `__context__` — automatic: set when an exception is raised inside `except`/`finally`.
- `__cause__` — explicit: set by `raise ... from ...`.
- `__traceback__` — the traceback object.

### Re-raise correctly

```python
try: ...
except SomeError:
    log()
    raise                                  # bare raise preserves traceback
```

sections.title: 4. Custom exceptions
sections.body:
```python
class DomainError(Exception):
    """Base for our domain errors."""

class NotFoundError(DomainError): ...

class ValidationError(DomainError):
    def __init__(self, field, msg):
        super().__init__(f"{field}: {msg}")
        self.field = field
        self.msg = msg
```

Design tips:

- **Always inherit from `Exception`**, never `BaseException`.
- Group with a base class so callers can catch the family.
- Add useful attributes (`field`, `code`, etc.).
- Keep messages actionable.
- Name ends in `Error` for errors, `Warning` for warnings.

sections.title: 5. EAFP vs LBYL
sections.body:
- **EAFP** (Easier to Ask Forgiveness than Permission) — Pythonic.
  ```python
  try: return d[k]
  except KeyError: return default
  ```
- **LBYL** (Look Before You Leap)
  ```python
  if k in d: return d[k]
  return default
  ```
  Risk: race condition between check and use (`os.path.exists` then `open`).

EAFP is preferred when:

- Race conditions exist.
- The "happy path" is overwhelmingly common.
- The check is expensive or duplicative.

LBYL is fine for:

- Cheap, definitive checks (`isinstance`, `len`).
- When you don't want exception cost.

sections.title: 6. Exception cost & performance
sections.body:
- Raising is expensive (builds traceback). Cost-free if you don't raise.
- For hot paths with many expected misses, prefer LBYL or `dict.get`.
- For occasional errors, EAFP is fine and clearer.

sections.title: 7. Context managers as exception tools
8. finally traps
sections.body:
```python
def f():
    try: return 1
    finally: return 2          # returns 2; hides 1
```

Don't `return`/`raise` in `finally` unless intentional.

A new exception in `finally` _replaces_ the original (you can see original via `__context__`).

sections.title: 9. Exception groups & except* (3.11+)
sections.body:
For tasks that raise multiple errors (e.g., `asyncio.TaskGroup`).

```python
eg = ExceptionGroup("multiple", [ValueError("a"), TypeError("b")])

try: raise eg
except* ValueError as g: print("got value errors", g.exceptions)
except* TypeError as g:  print("got type errors", g.exceptions)
```

`except*` runs every matching branch (vs normal `except` which runs only the first match).

sections.title: 10. assert statement
sections.body:
```python
assert x > 0, "x must be positive"
```

- Raises `AssertionError`.
- **Disabled with `-O`** (optimized mode). Don't use for production input validation; use `raise ValueError`.
- Good for invariants in tests and debug code.

sections.title: 11. Logging exceptions properly
sections.body:
```python
import logging
log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
try: ...
except Exception:
    log.exception("ctx info")              # logs message + traceback at ERROR level
```

Don't `print(e)` — you lose the traceback. Don't `log.error(str(e))` either — same loss.

sections.title: 12. Warnings (related)
sections.body:
```python
import warnings
warnings.warn("deprecated", DeprecationWarning, stacklevel=2)
warnings.filterwarnings("error")           # turn warnings into exceptions
```

sections.title: 13. traceback module
sections.body:
```python
import traceback
try: ...
except Exception:
    traceback.print_exc()                  # to stderr
    s = traceback.format_exc()             # as string
```

sections.title: 14. Anti-patterns to call out
sections.body:
- Bare `except:` or `except Exception: pass`.
- Swallowing exceptions silently.
- Catching exceptions just to re-raise a generic one (lose context).
- Using exceptions for normal flow on hot paths.
- Returning error codes/None instead of raising.
- Catching `Exception` at every layer (causes "exception laundering").
- Using `assert` for production validation.
